result.summary: Adds two USDT tracepoints to net_processing.cpp: net:block_header, which fires when a new valid header arrives via headers or cmpctblock, and net:compact_block_reconstructed, which fires with per-peer, per-source (prefilled/mempool/extra-pool/requested) transaction counts when a compact block is successfully reconstructed. A small blockencodings.cpp/.h refactor factors the existing debug-log statistics computation into a reusable GetReconstructionStats() used by both the log line and the new tracepoint. Includes doc/tracing.md documentation and a substantial functional test (test/functional/interface_usdt_net.py) exercising both tracepoints.
result.problem: Compact block relay performance (mempool overlap, extra-pool usefulness, per-peer reconstruction success) is currently observable only through unstructured debug logs, which are hard to consume programmatically for continuous measurement or tooling built by operators and researchers running dashboards over node internals.

open_concerns: 0xB10C and stickies-v suggested it might make more sense to first resolve the structured-logging (#35369) or IPC tracing (#35142) direction rather than add more ad hoc USDT tracepoints now; no further reply from either after the author's rebuttal.
m4ycon suggested also exposing the missing txids from vtx_missing for deeper diagnosis; 0xB10C noted lists/sets are impractical to pass via tracepoints and this was left out of scope.
resolved_concerns: Author (w0xlt) argued IPC tracing is a longer-term project not ready to replace USDT tracing today, and this is a small incremental addition; no further objection followed.

categories.evidence: Adds tracepoints and a small stats-computation refactor inside src/net_processing.cpp and src/blockencodings.cpp/.h, in the compact block relay and header-processing code paths (ProcessCompactBlockTxns, LogBlockHeader, ProcessMessage).
categories.rationale: It does not change relay behavior, correctness, or resource use; it only exposes existing computed data via inert USDT probes (design note: 'nothing new is computed in the hot path'). Its value is diagnostic: m4ycon described a real production case where compact block reconstructions unexpectedly required round trips and lacked the data to investigate, which this PR would help with going forward. Reviewers flagged an open question of whether this duplicates effort better spent on a structured-logging or IPC-tracing interface, which affects direction more than urgency.

uncertainties: Whether the project wants more ad hoc USDT tracepoints added while #35369 (structured logging) and #35142 (IPC tracing RFC) are unresolved is a live strategic question that could change this PR's priority for the p2p category once settled.
No indication of how many external tools (peer-observer or others) are actively waiting on these specific tracepoints beyond m4ycon's referenced dashboard work.
result.card: This PR adds two USDT tracepoints, net:block_header and net:compact_block_reconstructed, giving operators structured, low-overhead visibility into compact block relay: which peer announced a header and how a reconstruction split across prefilled, mempool, extra-pool, and requested transactions. It solves a real diagnostic gap: reviewer m4ycon described running dashboards (peer-observer) and hitting periods of unexplained round-trip requests with no structured data to investigate why. Concept ACKs came from 0xB10C and m4ycon, though both suggested first clarifying whether a structured-logging interface (#35369) or the IPC tracing RFC (#35142) should supersede ad hoc tracepoints like this; the author rebutted that IPC tracing is not a near-term substitute, and neither reviewer pushed back further. The PR needs rebase and the author has been silent for over 100 days, including through a maintainer's rebase request, so it is currently Stale. The change is purely observational, touching no relay logic or behavior, so its priority in p2p is moderate rather than critical.
